headline: Researchers from Rutgers, IBM and partner institutions showed that a quantum computer can check and reset its own qubits mid-calculation across a chain of up to 100 qubits.
score_reason: Peer-reviewed result but a research step, and reported from 12 Oct; lowered by 1 as older news.
importance_line: Quantum researchers get evidence for the real-time self-correction that future reliable machines need, though no fault-tolerant quantum computer exists yet.
summary: AZoQuantum reports, as 12 Oct coverage of a Nature Physics study, that researchers from Rutgers, IBM, City College of New York and other institutions used a 156-qubit IBM processor to run nearly 10,000 combined scrambling and reset operations, the largest such demonstration to date. The team saw a sharp tipping point from chaos to order depending on how often qubits were reset, a step toward the continuous error correction that fault-tolerant machines will need.
notes: CCNY release and Phys.org blocked; AZoQuantum read. Our first edition carrying it, but event predates 14 Oct.
